bridge_state.source_integration: hcli.repo_context uses one hawking-gravityd child when HCLI_NATIVE_GRAVITY=1; hcli.serve enables that only for its daemon-owned process and prewarms the child during resident startup. HCLI lake.catalog adopts the same native child for exact catalog queries, with a schema-checked catalog-file compatibility fallback only. ToolRegistry.invoke uses the same child as an additional fail-closed tool name/mutation/permission admission fence before Python schema validation and handlers. The canonical fs.list handler uses the child for contained, bounded, content-free discovery and retains the Python os.walk implementation only as a compatibility fallback. The canonical fs.search handler uses the resident bounded text index for contained searches and retains its exact Python walker as a compatibility fallback. Path-shaped RepoContext queries use native resident path ranking; explicitly named relative files take a containment-checked direct fast lane, while non-exact path queries retain directory freshness validation. Content-oriented RepoContext queries use one native multi-term rank request when available and retain the rg/content fallback otherwise.

migration_law: Port a stable Python owner into Rust with a differential/parity fixture before retiring it.
The release path must call a persistent native owner, not spawn a Rust subprocess per request.
Every hot migration needs a measured before/after wall-time receipt; Rust syntax alone earns no performance claim.
Odyssey remains active while this census advances in parallel; new native owners still require a working resident bridge, differential parity, and measured before/after evidence.
